q8.answer: Counts live in one shared Redis (primary/replica), keyed per customer and minute as rl:{customerId}:{floor(now/60)}, so every gateway instance reads and writes the same counter. Each key expires after 120 s, which removes old counts.

q9.answer: Budget resets when the wall-clock minute rolls over: a fixed one-minute window aligned to the clock, so the next window uses a new key starting at zero. There is no gradual or sliding recovery; the old key just expires. This allows up to a 2x burst across a boundary, accepted for v1.

q10.answer: A single Redis Lua script does the check and count atomically on the store: read the count, return DENIED without incrementing if count >= limit, otherwise INCR (EXPIRE on first hit) and return ALLOWED. Because Redis runs the script as one step, two instances cannot both take the last slot. It uses the Redis server clock (TIME), not gateway clocks.

q11.answer: Retry-After is ceil(secondsLeftInWindow), where secondsLeftInWindow = 60 - (now mod 60), computed in the script from the Redis clock, with a minimum of 1. It is the time until the current fixed window ends and the counter resets.

q12.answer: No retry: the gateway waits at most 50 ms, then on error or timeout forwards the request, emits the ratelimit_store_unavailable metric, and uses no local fallback counter. The client gets the normal backend response with status unchanged and no X-RateLimit-Limit or X-RateLimit-Remaining headers, since the real count is unknown.
